record.body:
## Architecture

`dashboard/web/app.py` drops `from __future__ import annotations`. Route functions defined inside `create_app` keep their current signatures, including `request: Request` on POST `/api/needs` and POST `/api/backlog`. Annotations evaluate in that function's local scope, where `Request`, `JSONResponse`, and `HTMLResponse` are imported. FastAPI then treats `request` as the HTTP request, and `await request.json()` reads the body. The stdlib handler in `dashboard/web/service.py` is unchanged.

## Interfaces

POST `/api/backlog` and POST `/api/needs` accept a JSON object body and no query string. Bodies stay `{id, action, effort?, note?, revision?}`. Responses stay `{"ok": true}` or `{"error": "..."}` from `WriteError`. GET `/openapi.json` returns the generated schema.

## Decisions

web-write-annotation: drop postponed annotations in `dashboard/web/app.py`.
web-write-body-grouping: phase is ungrouped.

## Invariants

`fastapi` is imported only inside `create_app`. Write handlers still delegate to `Reader.write_needs` and `Reader.write_backlog`.

## Assumptions

Postponed annotations are the only reason FastAPI treats `request` as a query parameter. A process that imported `dashboard.web.app` before this change must be restarted to pick it up.

## Tradeoffs

The file can no longer postpone annotations. A later local import used only in a type hint would need a real import at definition time. That is the same rule the rest of the module already follows once the future import is gone.

## Risks

An already-running `dashboard/bin/web` process keeps the broken app until it is restarted. Tests that only drive `dashboard.web.serve` would still miss a regression, so the new test must use the FastAPI app.
